money.note: Individuals gave $1,189,057; PAC money $219,249; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Democrat and Los Angeles County Supervisor for District 1 since 2014. Former U.S. Secretary of Labor (2009–2013), U.S. Representative (2001–2009), California state senator and assemblywoman, and Rio Hondo College trustee. Member-elect for California's 38th Congressional District.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions from Solis on data centers, development or growth limits as a county supervisor, homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign land buyers, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we had no campaign platform page. The Wikipedia article we read was cut off before its coverage of her Labor Secretary years and her time on the Board of Supervisors, so we left out anything from those periods. No foreign ties were documented in the pages we read.

qual.why: She has held legislative office at the state and federal level, served in a cabinet-level executive post, and sits on a county board that sets budgets, which fits the rubric's top band.

cands.name: Pedro Antonio Casas
cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army colonel with about 29 years of service and a Ph.D. in counseling psychology. He is a clinical, forensic and aero-medical psychologist who commanded medical detachments in Iraq and Afghanistan. He has not held elected office. He ran for Congress in 2024 (District 31) and 2026 (District 38).

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California endorsed him in the 2024 District 31 race, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no independent news coverage of Casas, so his birthplace, upbringing, education and military career come only from his own campaign website. We found no stated position on data centers, development, growth limits, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, guns, or abortion. His site mentions tax cuts and less regulation in general terms but nothing specific to property taxes. He has not held elected office, so there are no official actions to report. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had. Ballotpedia lists 2026 voter-guide endorsements from informal groups, which we left out as not notable.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was born in El Paso, Texas, in 1962 and moved to Baldwin Park, California, where he attended kindergarten through 8th grade and then Don Bosco Technical Institute, graduating in 1981.

score.why: Raised $0, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He served about 29 years in the U.S. Army, retiring as a colonel in September 2023. He was a division psychologist in South Korea, commanded medical detachments in Iraq and Afghanistan and units in Germany, and was chief of behavioral health departments at medical centers in Honolulu and Washington, D.C. He has no legislative or elected experience.
qual.why: Long military command and department-management experience puts him in the middle band for executive management. He has no prior legislative, budget or elected office, which keeps him from the high band. All of this comes from his own campaign site.
qual.label: Long military command and department-management experience puts him in the middle band for executive management. He has no prior legislative, budget or elected office, which keeps him from the high band. All of this comes from his own campaign site.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Lists support for implementing private school vouchers among his local priorities. His site does not mention teacher pay.

back-police-order.evidence: Lists supporting law enforcement and opposing any defunding measures among his national priorities. He also calls for a justice system that does not reward criminal behavior and for restoring order.

workers-first.evidence: Pledges to secure the southern border and pursue immigration reforms that prioritize national security. His site does not mention H-1B visas, E-Verify or deportation policy.
